sec: Dengue critical phase: capillary leak, monitoring, platelet thresholds, day-wise chart

items.q: Which days are printed as the most crucial period of dengue?
Critical-phase problems — match — 1) Bleeding 2) Capillary leak … A) Pleural or pericardial effusion and ascites B) Falling platelet count
items.exp: 'In some patients : ↓ Platelet count (Bleeding), Capillary leak syndrome (Pleural / pericardial effusion, ascites)'. (Book p1056)

items.q: How is capillary leak syndrome manifested, according to the page?
opts: Pleural or pericardial effusion and ascites
items.exp: 'Capillary leak syndrome (Pleural / pericardial effusion, ascites)'. (Book p1056)

items.q: Monitoring in the critical phase — match — 1) Circulation 2) Volume status 3) Haemoconcentration … A) IVC diameter B) Haematocrit C) Blood pressure supported with IV fluids
items.exp: 'monitor and maintenance : · BP by I/V fluids, · IVC diameter, · Hematocrit'. (Book p1056)

items.q: What platelet thresholds does the page print for transfusing platelets in dengue?
opts: Below 50,000, or below 1 lakh with bleeding

items.q: What does the page print about steroids in dengue?
Judge the management block: I Monitoring covers blood pressure, IVC diameter and haematocrit. II Steroids have no role.
items.exp: Both statements reproduce 'monitor and maintenance' and 'No use of steroids'. (Book p1056)

items.q: Course of illness phases — match — 1) Early 2) Critical 3) Late … A) Febrile B) Recovery C) Critical
items.exp: 'Course of illness : Febrile, Critical, Recovery phases'. (Book p1056)

items.q: Day-wise chart — match the column to its content — 1) Temperature 2) Potential clinical issues 3) Lab changes 4) Serology and virology … A) Dehydration, shock and bleeding, then reabsorption and fluid overload, organ impairment, platelets B) IgM and IgG, viraemia C) Haematocrit D) Up to 40°C
items.exp: The chart rows are 'Days of illness 1-10', 'Temperature' (40°), 'Potential clinical issues' (dehydration, shock/bleeding, reabsorption/fluid overload, organ impairment, platelet), 'Lab changes' (haematocrit), 'Serology and virology' (IgM/IgG, viraemia) and 'Course of illness' (febrile, critical, recovery). (Book p1056)

items.q: Fill up: 'Note : IgM becomes positive from day ______ onwards.'
items.exp: 'Note : IgM become positive : Day 5 onwards'. (Book p1056)

items.q: Which warning-sign group is contrasted with 'dengue without warning signs' on this spread?
opts: Dengue with warning signs / organ failure
items.exp: 'Dengue with warning signs/organ failure' is the label under the critical-period branch. (Book p1056)

items.q: On day 6 of dengue a patient develops ascites, a falling haematocrit and a platelet count of 15,000 with mucosal bleeding. Which printed intervention applies?
opts: Transfuse platelets, since the count is below 20,000 with bleeding
No transfusion, since the count is above 10,000
items.exp: The threshold is 'Administer if < 10,000 OR < 20,000 + bleeding'. (Book p1056)
